text:
Krung Non Market is a fairly large market. The outdoor area sells new and second-hand clothing, shoes, bed sheets, 10-baht household items, and second-hand goods displayed on sheets for customers to browse.
The central area features outdoor food stalls where vendors set up their own tents, which is quite lively with many people buying food. This zone also has a ball pit for children to play in (coupons available).
Inside the covered area, you'll find mobile phone shops, vegetable stalls, bakeries, and flower garland vendors. These are permanently located shops that operate daily.
Most customers are residents of the Taling Chan area and migrant workers from neighboring countries, who come to shop in large numbers.
Parking is available on the sides and behind the market, with designated parking areas, and it's free.
There's a mobile sound system from Wat Phra Bat Nam Phu promoting the temple's products under the brand name "Jai Fah," including fabric softener, laundry detergent, dishwashing liquid, inhalers, balm, riceberry rice, and more. The money will go towards taking care of underprivileged or orphaned children who are currently under the care of the temple. So, my mother took the opportunity to buy Jai Fah products because it's a buy-one-get-two deal: she gets the product to use and also does good deeds at the same time.
My mother said that if she lived around here, she would come to the market every day because she could buy everything she needed in one place.
I like this place because the vegetables are fresh and cheap (3 bags for 50 baht). There's parking available, and sometimes there's a market with reasonably priced fruit.
